extracted.intended_audience: academic researchers and policy analysts studying the causal effect of patents on startup outcomes (empirical economists, applied microeconomists, IO/innovation scholars)
extracted.subtask_description: Econometric/empirical protocol for estimating how approval of a startup’s patent application affects subsequent outcomes (employment, sales, survival, follow-on innovation, financing). Uses examiner leniency as an instrument in 2SLS with multiple robustness checks and sample restrictions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Instrument: past examiner approval rate
rubrics_metrics.description: Use the past approval rate of the patent examiner in charge of reviewing a startup’s first patent application to predict whether the application will be approved (first-stage of 2SLS).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Identification assumes applications are assigned to examiners quasi-randomly within an art unit and year. The first stage is estimated in various specifications (columns 1–6) and the approval-rate instrument is reported along with standard errors and significance. The instrument is also used for second (and subsequent) application analyses (e.g., examiner approval rate of second application).

rubrics_metrics.name: Quasi-random assignment identification assumption
rubrics_metrics.description: Identification assumes that patent applications are assigned to examiners quasi-randomly within an art unit and year, allowing examiner-specific past approval rates to serve as an instrument for approval.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Threats to this assumption are investigated by controlling for applicant/application characteristics (to rule out quality-based assignment) and examiner characteristics and by including more granular fixed effects (technology-subclass-by-year). Instrument validity is further tested by regressing examiner approval rate on applicant, application, and examiner characteristics (Table 3). Columns restrict samples (e.g., filings also to EPO/JPO) to probe validity.

rubrics_metrics.name: Fixed effects and their role
rubrics_metrics.description: Include art-unit-by-year fixed effects as baseline; additional specifications include tech-subclass-by-year and headquarter-state fixed effects.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Baseline specification includes art-unit-by-year fixed effects (to absorb art-unit × year assignment patterns). Columns 5 and 6 add tech-subclass-by-year fixed effects to control for examiner specialization. All second-stage specifications include art-unit-by-year and headquarter-state fixed effects (and sometimes subclass-by-year).

rubrics_metrics.name: Controls for applicant, application, and examiner characteristics
rubrics_metrics.description: Control for applicant characteristics (ln employees at filing/first-action, ln(1+sales), employment growth, sales growth), application characteristics (ln # independent claims), and examiner characteristics (ln examiner experience, examiner grade indicators GS-9–GS-15) to account for potential quality-based assignment.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Columns 2–4 investigate quality-based assignment using applicant/application characteristics. Columns 5–6 investigate assignment based on examiner characteristics, including proxies for experience and seniority. These additional controls are included in alternative first-stage specifications and (in Internet Appendix) in second stage as robustness.

rubrics_metrics.name: Estimation method: two-stage least squares (2SLS)
rubrics_metrics.description: Estimate causal effects by 2SLS using examiner approval rate as the instrument for application approval, with least squares used in all specifications.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: First-stage equation (3) is estimated in multiple specifications; second stage uses predicted approval. Results reported for employment growth, sales growth, survival, follow-on innovation, VC/IPO access, and collateral pledging. OLS variants are also reported as robustness (Internet Appendix).

rubrics_metrics.name: Weak-instrument test: Kleibergen-Paap rk Wald F statistic
rubrics_metrics.description: Use the Kleibergen-Paap rk Wald F statistic as the weak-instrument test for the 2SLS analyses.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Report the Kleibergen-Paap statistic (and F-test: IV = 0) for each column. Large values reported (e.g., 1,504.1*** in many specifications) indicate instrument strength. Diagnostics section of tables lists this statistic alongside R2 and observation counts.

rubrics_metrics.name: Standard errors: heteroskedasticity-consistent clustered at art-unit
rubrics_metrics.description: Report heteroskedasticity-consistent standard errors clustered at the art unit level underneath coefficient estimates.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Standard errors are shown in italics under coefficient estimates. Clustering at the art unit accounts for within-art-unit correlation in residuals; this is used throughout the paper's tables.

rubrics_metrics.name: Significance notation and two-sided tests
rubrics_metrics.description: Use ***, **, and * to denote significance at the 1%, 5%, and 10% level (two-sided), respectively.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: All reported coefficient significance follows this notation. Interpret coefficient estimates with corresponding significance markers and clustered standard errors.

rubrics_metrics.name: Outcome definitions: employment, sales growth, survival measurement windows
rubrics_metrics.description: Employment growth and sales growth measured over 1, 2, 3, 4, and 5 years following the USPTO first-action on the firm’s first patent application; survival modeled via linear probability of being alive in year t.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For startups that die, growth rate is set to –100% in the year of exit. Panel A controls for log employment at first-action; Panel B controls for log sales at first-action (not shown). NETS data provide employment and sales; startups not matchable to NETS are excluded. NETS data available through 2011, reducing sample window for longer horizons. Panels report 2SLS estimates for each horizon with diagnostics.

rubrics_metrics.name: Follow-on innovation metrics and measurement of citations
rubrics_metrics.description: Measure follow-on innovation via: log(1 + subsequent patent applications), log(1 + subsequent approved patents), approval rate of subsequent patent applications, log(1 + total citations to subsequent patent applications), and log(1 + avg. citations-per-patent to subsequent approved patents). Citations measured over five years following each patent’s public disclosure date (typically 18 months after filing).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Column-specific samples: column 3 includes only startups filing at least one patent after the first-action and for which approval rate can be measured; column 5 includes only startups with at least one subsequent patent approval and measurable avg citations-per-patent. Untabulated results note effects stronger when measuring citations over seven or ten years. All specifications estimated by 2SLS using examiner approval rate as instrument.

rubrics_metrics.name: Sample restrictions and subsample analyses
rubrics_metrics.description: Several analyses restrict samples depending on outcome availability or robustness needs (e.g., startups matchable to NETS, startups that file abroad, firms with/without prior VC).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples: sales/employment analyses exclude startups not matched to NETS; instrument validity columns 5–6 restrict to applications also filed with the European and Japanese patent offices; Table 9 splits samples by prior VC rounds, founder experience, state agglomeration, industry, and by whether first application was rejected. Columns interacting approval effects use interacted instruments (examiner approval rate × splitting variable).

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition of VC/IPO and debt outcome indicators
rubrics_metrics.description: VC access: dependent variable equals one if the startup raises VC funding at some point in the 1…5 years following the first-action decision; IPO indicator equals one if startup goes public after first-action. Debt access: indicator equals one if startup pledges its patent application as collateral in a security agreement (recorded as a patent reassignment) within 1…5 years or at any future point.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Panel A (all firms) and Panel B (firms without VC funding) reported separately for debt analyses. Median months from first-action to VC round or IPO given for successful applicants. All specifications estimated by 2SLS with examiner approval rate instrument; diagnostics reported.

rubrics_metrics.name: Handling of second patent application analyses
rubrics_metrics.description: Repeat the main analyses (employment, sales, follow-on innovation) modeling the effect of approval of a startup’s second patent application, instrumenting with the examiner approval rate for the second application.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Second-application analyses use the same 2SLS framework, fixed effects, clustered SEs, and diagnostics (Kleibergen-Paap), and report both 2SLS and OLS variants. Panel C reports follow-on innovation for second application with sample restrictions analogous to first-application analyses.

rubrics_metrics.name: Instrument validity regression checks
rubrics_metrics.description: Assess instrument validity by regressing the examiner approval rate on applicant, application, and examiner characteristics to check for correlations that would violate exclusion/ignorability.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Table 3 reports such regressions; presence/absence of correlations across columns with different fixed effects informs plausibility of quasi-random assignment. Also check approval by foreign patent offices (EPO/JPO) as predictors of examiner approval rate.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reporting of estimation diagnostics and summary statistics
rubrics_metrics.description: Report diagnostics including R2, weak-instrument test statistic, unconditional mean of dependent variable, median/mean/standard deviation of key variables, and number of observations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Tables include these diagnostics beneath coefficient blocks. Summary statistics tables (e.g., Table 1) report means, medians, standard deviations for covariates and outcome windows. Use these diagnostics to assess precision, instrument strength, and sample size.

rubrics_metrics.name: Addressing potential confound from review speed
rubrics_metrics.description: Control for patent review speed to remove confound if lenient examiners are also faster and review speed independently affects outcomes; instrument review speed using administrative delay measures.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Instrument for review speed using the sum of time from filing to assignment to examiner docket (administrative delays unrelated to invention quality) plus the average time that examiner has taken in the past from docket to first-action, following Hegde and Ljungqvist (2017). Include this additional IV in 2SLS to isolate approval effect net of review speed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Coding of outcomes for firms that exit and exclusion rules
rubrics_metrics.description: For startups that die, set growth rate to –100% in the year of exit; startups not matched to NETS are excluded from growth analyses.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Sample reduces as horizon lengthens due to NETS coverage through 2011. For variable definitions and details of construction, refer to Appendix A (not shown). This coding choice affects measurement of employment/sales growth and survival analyses.
